# Selected staging producer trace

September 17 follow-on: the orchestrator selected Next as continuation owner and
Designs as authority. Local finalized-source and unresolved-intent adapters now
exist. Later read-only inspection found actual data-template, section and field
markers in the legacy shared-template family; any earlier blanket absence claim
is superseded by LEGACY-SHARED-SHELL-ADAPTER-2026-09-17.md. Missing authored
content/rights/mappings remain distinct from available structural boundaries.

Local source investigation after the independent parent retest. No production
records or secrets were read, and no generator, callback or hosting operation
was invoked. The agency source is 92e0d4b; Next code is 118201e (handoff 1e678ad).

## Actual normal path

Agency `SiteStudioProofClient` dispatches a proof request. The legacy Studio
`server/famtastic-proof-job-routes.js` calls its existing generator, retains
generated variants for retries, packages their HTML, and sends each variant's
`design_dna` unchanged. In legacy `server.js`, the generator writes
`proof_id`, `direction_id`, `direction_name`, `generated_at`,
`generation_time_ms`, `spec_snapshot`, `style_fingerprint`, `layout_variant`,
`font_pairing`, `template_path`, `artifact_path`, `thumbnail`,
`media_fulfillment` and `content_verification`.

Agency `ProofCampaignService::acceptCallbackInternal` validates HTML and assets,
writes protected bytes, replaces the upstream asset list with its own
`asset_manifest`, and persists Design DNA on the proof variant. This is proof
finalization, not complete-site finalization. The deterministic pilot writes
an even smaller palette/typography/layout record. The retired Locs packaging
script is check-only and its historical candidate metadata is not a site
completion contract. Its separate customer source must not be reconstructed.

`CustomerPortalService::createSelectedProofStaging` rehashes selected HTML,
checks every protected asset against the recorded manifest, and passes the
DNA to `SelectedStagingContinuation::createPacket`. That serializer requires
`selected_build_continuation`. No normal agency writer currently supplies it.
The hand-seeded positive harness proves the consumer boundary only.

Next `prepareStagingLockIn` and `prepareStagingBuildPacket` consume an already
authoritative selection/spec/design/research/artifact snapshot. They are not
writers of agency scope or rights truth. The ordinary Next pipeline returns
its research packet, derived spec, composed pages and verification result;
there is no agency proof-finalization callback in Next. P0-I1 prohibits moving
the legacy three-proof handler into Next as an implicit fix.

## Exact facts and owners

| Continuation fact | Recorded source available now | Missing writer or binding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Request/customer/project/campaign and selected variant | Agency request, project and variant records | Derivable at actual selection; do not ask an operator to duplicate these IDs. |
| Source path, SHA-256, length, asset inventory | Agency protected HTML and validated `asset_manifest` | Derivable at selection; byte identity does not establish site completeness. |
| Direction name and generation provenance | Variant DNA / legacy `spec_snapshot`, proof ID and time | Derivable without regeneration; retain original provenance. |
| `spec.capability_class`, `required_pages`, completion versus remaining work | Intake captures requested pages/integrations; legacy `spec_snapshot` describes a proof | Agency scope service must bind agreed scope to the request; source finalizer must attest which required pages are actually complete. Neither generated HTML nor recommendation SKU is that attestation. |
| `brand.design_contract` | Legacy style fingerprint, fonts, layout and template path | Source/design finalizer must export a validated contract matching the selected source; these partial fields cannot safely supply all canonical tokens, layout, responsive and evolution rules. |
| `research_packet_ref` | Next research packet exists for Next builds; verified-cold agency Build DNA has a separately registered immutable manifest | Bind the exact research/brief record to the selected artifact. Generic legacy proof callback does not supply that reference; do not invent it from a proof ID. |
| Per-file `rights.status` / `evidence_ref` | Media fulfillment records generated provider, prompt and relative image path; verified-cold Build DNA has an asset ledger | Media/source rights owner must supply a real approval record bound to each file. `fulfilled`, generated bytes or a signed download are not rights approval. |
| File HTTPS URLs usable by the worker | Agency signed proof reader and protected filesystem inventory | Artifact delivery owner must implement/bind the worker-authenticated immutable retrieval route. Existing browser preview URL is not automatically a byte endpoint. |
| `hosting_target` URL/path/subdirectory | Next deployment planner can plan targets; agency final-release service has a different release target | Review-host registry must persist the authoritative per-project protected Inc binding. Do not repurpose final-release hosting or guess a production target from a slug. |
| Continuation recipe for missing work | Narrow Next `selected-html-slots-v1` executor | Source finalizer must supply exact selected-template and approved missing-page slot inputs. General revisions/application execution remains unsupported. |

The verified-cold path also records full Build DNA transactionally through
`acceptVerifiedColdCallback` / `BuildTelemetryService::recordBuildDna`; that
record is a useful provenance source, but registration alone does not prove
agreed scope is materialized or allocate protected review hosting.

## Resolution boundary

There is no evidence-backed positive routine producer fixture using the
unmodified existing legacy output: necessary authority-bearing facts are
absent. Supplying them under new fixture keys would only rename hand-seeding.
The safe existing behavior remains a durable selected intent plus exception.
This is an implementation gap, not a configuration-only activation gate.

The required owner decision is whether to extend the existing legacy source
finalizer in a new isolated worktree, or introduce a separately owned source
finalization service in the customer-source lane. Either choice also needs
the agency scope/rights/review-target writers above. It must preserve the
selected bytes, perform no fresh research/redesign, and keep the three-concept
proof lifecycle separate from complete-site packaging. Pending this decision,
no hollow producer bridge or positive end-to-end readiness claim was added.
